new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and predictable: default on the penultimate syllable (e.g. ['ol.ki] 'heavy', [pla'ko.lu] 'young man'), but a heavy final syllable (vowel sequence VV or closed VC) attracts stress to the final syllable ([i'pir] 'hot', [ka'pou] 'large', [a.nan.ki'ao] 'excellent'); if the (final) third syllable is an onsetless bare V, stress retracts to the antepenult (['no.wi.ə] 'another'). Verbs: penult on verbs of <=3 syllables with only a realis suffix, final if heavy; 4+-syllable verbs with realis suffix take antepenult; adding any prefix to a 2-3 syllable verb moves stress penult->antepenult; a disyllabic suffix puts stress on the suffix's first syllable (word penult), a monosyllabic suffix leaves stress unchanged.
new_statements.exceptions: Two-syllable numerals ('one'..'five') are stressed on the last syllable (sec. 4.2); in their longer forms stress is again penultimate. Verb prefixation/suffixation conditions in sec. 4.1.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the (inflected) word; examples are citation forms with morpheme breaks marked; stress marked with ' before the stressed syllable. Authors state stress is predictable (non-phonemic).
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Namia as a whole (informants from Yaru, Yegarapi and Norambalip villages, Edwaki area, Lumi Sub-District); authors state 'language differences are minimal' across the four social areas. Same language as glottocode nami1256 / ISO nnm; no separate dialect glottocode needed.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Default stress on the penultimate syllable of the word (including inflected non-verbs). A final syllable with a heavy core (VV or VC) attracts stress (e.g. /ipir/ [i'pir] 'hot', /kapou/ [ka'pou] 'large', /a.nan.kiao/ [a.nan.ki'ao] 'excellent'). If the penult is an onsetless light V, stress retracts to the antepenult (/no.wi.e/ ['no.wi.e] 'another'). Verbs: penult on stems of up to three syllables with only a realis suffix; heavy final still wins; four-plus-syllable verbs with only a realis suffix take antepenultimate stress; adding a prefix of any length to two- or three-syllable verbs moves stress from penult to antepenult; a two-syllable suffix pulls stress onto the penult (first suffix syllable), a one-syllable suffix leaves it unchanged. Stress is entirely predictable, so it is non-contrastive.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned; the work only marks one stress per word and gives no statement on secondary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Two-syllable numerals ('two', 'three', 'four', 'five') carry final stress; their longer, more common forms revert to penultimate stress (p.18, sec. 4.2). Verb stress depends on prefix/suffix morphology as described (pp.17-18).
new_statements.identity_note: The work covers Namia as spoken in the Edwaki area, Lumi Sub-District, Sandaun Province, with informants from Yaru, Yegarapi and Norambalip villages; the authors state that the four social areas differ minimally in language, so no dialect qualification is needed.
